lessons.title: India's SDG Monitoring Framework
lessons.content_md:
# India's SDG Monitoring Framework

## The 2030 Agenda

In 2015, all 193 UN member states adopted the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development** — a blueprint for peace and prosperity built around **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, **169 targets**, and **231 unique indicators**.

## MoSPI's Role

MoSPI is the **nodal ministry** for SDG indicator monitoring in India. The NSO:

- Maintains the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** — India's localized version of the global SDG indicators
- Publishes the **SDG India Index** (in collaboration with NITI Aayog)
- Coordinates data flows from 50+ ministries and state statistical bureaus

## National Indicator Framework (NIF)

| Feature | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Total indicators | 306 (as of latest revision) |
| Data sources | NSS, Census, Administrative records, Ministry MIS |
| Review cycle | Annual review by the Statistical Coordination Committee |
| Classification | Tier I (data available), Tier II (methodology exists, no data), Tier III (no methodology) |

## SDG India Index

Published by **NITI Aayog** using MoSPI data:

- Ranks all **36 states/UTs** on SDG performance
- Composite score: 0 (worst) to 100 (best)
- Categories: Aspirant (0-49), Performer (50-64), Front Runner (65-99), Achiever (100)

## Key Statistical SDGs

| SDG | MoSPI Relevance |
|-----|------------------|
| SDG 1 (No Poverty) | Poverty estimation via NSS consumer expenditure |
| SDG 8 (Decent Work) | PLFS employment & unemployment data |
| SDG 9 (Industry) | ASI industrial statistics |
| SDG 10 (Inequalities) | Gini coefficient from NSS data |

lessons.title: Data Gaps & Tier Classification
lessons.content_md:
# Data Gaps & Tier Classification

## The Tier System

The UN Inter-Agency Expert Group on SDGs (IAEG-SDGs) classifies indicators into tiers based on data availability:

### Tier I
- **Methodology**: Internationally established
- **Data**: Regularly produced by at least 50% of countries
- **Example**: Under-5 mortality rate (SDG 3.2.1)

### Tier II
- **Methodology**: Internationally established
- **Data**: NOT regularly produced by countries
- **Example**: Proportion of youth not in education, employment, or training (SDG 8.6.1)

### Tier III (Eliminated in 2020)
- **Methodology**: Not yet established
- All former Tier III indicators have been reclassified or deleted

## India's Data Gaps

Despite having a strong statistical system, India faces challenges:

### Frequency Gaps
- Consumer Expenditure Survey: Last published 2011-12 (2017-18 was junked)
- Time Use Survey: Conducted only once (2019)

### Coverage Gaps
- Informal sector employment: Difficult to capture in establishment surveys
- Migration data: PLFS captures some, but internal migration is underestimated

### Disaggregation Gaps
- SDGs require data disaggregated by gender, age, disability, geography
- Many indicators only available at national/state level, not district

## Addressing Gaps

MoSPI strategies:

1. **Administrative Data Integration**: Use GST, EPFO, and NREGASoft data to supplement surveys
2. **Big Data/AI**: Satellite imagery for poverty mapping, mobile data for migration
3. **Coordination**: State Statistical Bureaus strengthened under the National Statistical Commission
4. **Capacity Building**: Training programs for statistical officers at NSSTA

lessons.title: Statistical Quality & International Standards
lessons.content_md:
# Statistical Quality & International Standards

## UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics

Adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2014, these 10 principles guide all national statistical offices:

1. **Relevance, impartiality, and equal access** — Statistics serve the public good
2. **Professional standards and ethics** — Methods follow scientific principles
3. **Accountability and transparency** — Sources and methods are published
4. **Prevention of misuse** — Statisticians may comment on misinterpretation
5. **Cost-effectiveness** — Resources used efficiently
6. **Confidentiality** — Individual data is strictly protected
7. **Legislation** — Statistical laws provide the framework
8. **Coordination** — Consistency across agencies
9. **International standards** — Follow UN/OECD guidelines
10. **International cooperation** — Bilateral and multilateral exchange

## India's Statistical Legislation

### Collection of Statistics Act, 2008
- Empowers the central government to collect statistics on any subject
- Penalizes false or misleading information
- Ensures confidentiality of individual responses

### National Statistical Commission (NSC)
- Advisory body on statistical quality and methodology
- Reviews survey designs, sampling frames, and estimation procedures
- Recommends improvements to the statistical system

## Data Quality Dimensions

| Dimension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Relevance** | Does the data meet user needs? |
| **Accuracy** | How close are estimates to true values? |
| **Timeliness** | Is data available when needed? |
| **Accessibility** | Can users easily find and use the data? |
| **Coherence** | Are different statistics consistent? |
| **Interpretability** | Is metadata adequate for proper use? |

## SDDS Plus

India subscribes to the IMF's **Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus (SDDS Plus)** — the highest tier of data transparency, requiring:
- Advance release calendars
- Specified coverage and periodicity
- Public access to methodology documentation
